WITH response_base AS (
    SELECT response_id, survey_id, duration_in_seconds, progress, is_finished
    FROM staging.stg_qualtrics__survey_response
    WHERE duration_in_seconds IS NOT NULL
      AND progress IS NOT NULL
),
quality_labels AS (
    SELECT
        *,
        CASE
            WHEN duration_in_seconds < 30 THEN 'Too Fast'
            WHEN duration_in_seconds > 3600 THEN 'Too Slow'
            WHEN duration_in_seconds BETWEEN 120 AND 1800 THEN 'Optimal'
            ELSE 'Suboptimal'
        END AS timing_quality,
        CASE
            WHEN is_finished IS TRUE AND progress >= 0.95 AND duration_in_seconds BETWEEN 60 AND 3600 THEN 'High Quality'
            WHEN is_finished IS TRUE AND progress >= 0.8 THEN 'Good Quality'
            WHEN progress >= 0.5 THEN 'Fair Quality'
            ELSE 'Poor Quality'
        END AS overall_quality_rating
    FROM response_base
)
SELECT
    response_id,
    survey_id,
    duration_in_seconds,
    progress,
    is_finished,
    timing_quality,
    overall_quality_rating,
    CASE overall_quality_rating
        WHEN 'High Quality' THEN 90
        WHEN 'Good Quality' THEN 75
        WHEN 'Fair Quality' THEN 60
        ELSE 30
    END::INTEGER AS quality_score,
    (is_finished IS TRUE AND progress >= 0.8 AND duration_in_seconds BETWEEN 30 AND 7200) AS include_in_analysis,
    current_timestamp AS analysis_date
FROM quality_labels

- name: int_qualtrics__response_quality
      description: 'Per-response quality metrics computed from Qualtrics staging data: timing category, overall rating, numeric score, analysis inclusion flag, and run timestamp'
      grain: One row per staging survey response with non-null duration_in_seconds and progress
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_qualtrics__survey_response
      business_logic: '- Start from staging.stg_qualtrics__survey_response using fields: response_id, survey_id, duration_in_seconds, progress, is_finished. - Filter out rows where duration_in_seconds OR progress is NULL; no other filtering, joins, ordering, or deduplication is applied. - Compute timing_quality from duration_in_seconds using inclusive thresholds where stated: - "Too Fast" if duration_in_seconds < 30 - "Too Slow" if duration_in_seconds > 3600 - "Optimal" if duration_in_seconds between 120 and 1800 inclusive - "Suboptimal" otherwise (covers 30–119 and 1801–3600, inclusive of 30 and 3600) - Compute overall_quality_rating with ordered precedence (first match wins): - "High Quality" if is_finished is true AND progress >= 0.95 AND duration_in_seconds between 60 and 3600 inclusive - "Good Quality" if is_finished is true AND progress >= 0.8 - "Fair Quality" if progress >= 0.5 - "Poor Quality" otherwise Note: is_finished NULL does not satisfy the true condition (no coercion). - Compute quality_score with the same conditions and precedence as overall_quality_rating: - 90 for "High Quality", 75 for "Good Quality", 60 for "Fair Quality", 30 for "Poor Quality". - Set include_in_analysis = true only if is_finished is true AND progress >= 0.8 AND duration_in_seconds between 30 and 7200 inclusive; else false. - Set analysis_date to the execution time using the environment’s current timestamp; same value for all rows in a run. - Output the original fields plus the derived fields; no aggregations, and duplicate response_id values (if present in staging) are preserved.'
      columns:
      - name: response_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Identifier of the survey response from staging; may repeat if the source contains duplicates
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: survey_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Identifier of the survey to which the response belongs (passed through from staging; may be NULL)
      - name: duration_in_seconds
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Response duration in seconds from staging; non-null due to filter; used for threshold comparisons only
      - name: progress
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Completion fraction from staging; non-null due to filter; compared against 0.5, 0.8, and 0.95 thresholds
      - name: is_finished
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: Staging completion flag; may be NULL; NULL does not satisfy true in condition checks
      - name: timing_quality
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Timing category from duration_in_seconds: ''Too Fast''(<30), ''Too Slow''(>3600), ''Optimal''(120–1800 inclusive), else ''Suboptimal'''
      - name: overall_quality_rating
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Ordered evaluation: High if finished and progress>=0.95 and duration 60–3600; else Good if finished and progress>=0.8; else Fair if progress>=0.5; else Poor'
      - name: quality_score
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: 'Score mapped from rating rules: 90 (High), 75 (Good), 60 (Fair), 30 (Poor)'
      - name: include_in_analysis
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: True only if finished and progress>=0.8 and duration_in_seconds between 30 and 7200 inclusive; otherwise false
      - name: analysis_date
        data_type: TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
        description: Execution timestamp assigned to all rows in the run using the environment’s current timestamp

        try_strptime(survey_response_recorded_at, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f %z')::TIMESTAMP AS recorded_at,

        distribution_channel,

    FROM response_rows
    WHERE recorded_at IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY date_trunc('day', recorded_at)
),
sent_events AS (
    SELECT
        try_strptime(distribution_contact.sent_at, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f %z')::TIMESTAMP AS sent_at,
        distribution_contact.contact_id,
        distribution_contact.opened_at,
        distribution_contact.response_started_at,
        distribution_contact.response_completed_at
    FROM staging.stg_qualtrics__distribution_contact AS distribution_contact
),
distribution_daily AS (
    SELECT
        date_trunc('day', sent_at) AS date_day,
        count(DISTINCT contact_id) FILTER (WHERE sent_at IS NOT NULL)::BIGINT AS count_contacts_sent_surveys,
        count(DISTINCT contact_id) FILTER (WHERE sent_at IS NOT NULL AND opened_at IS NOT NULL)::BIGINT AS count_contacts_opened_sent_surveys,
        count(DISTINCT contact_id) FILTER (WHERE sent_at IS NOT NULL AND response_started_at IS NOT NULL)::BIGINT AS count_contacts_started_sent_surveys,

    FROM sent_events

    GROUP BY date_trunc('day', sent_at)
),
contact_events AS (
    SELECT
        date_trunc('day', created_at) AS date_day,
        count(DISTINCT contact_id)::BIGINT AS count_contacts_created
    FROM staging.stg_qualtrics__directory_contact
    WHERE created_at IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY date_trunc('day', created_at)
),
unsubscribe_directory_daily AS (
    SELECT
        date_trunc('day', unsubscribed_from_directory_at) AS date_day,
        count(DISTINCT contact_id)::BIGINT AS count_contacts_unsubscribed_from_directory
    FROM staging.stg_qualtrics__directory_contact
    WHERE unsubscribed_from_directory_at IS NOT NULL AND is_unsubscribed_from_directory IS TRUE
    GROUP BY date_trunc('day', unsubscribed_from_directory_at)
),
unsubscribe_mailing_list_daily AS (
    SELECT
        date_trunc('day', unsubscribed_at) AS date_day,
        count(DISTINCT contact_id)::BIGINT AS count_contacts_unsubscribed_from_mailing_list
    FROM staging.stg_qualtrics__contact_mailing_list_membership
    WHERE unsubscribed_at IS NOT NULL AND is_unsubscribed IS TRUE
    GROUP BY date_trunc('day', unsubscribed_at)
),
spine_bounds AS (
    SELECT coalesce(min(date_trunc('day', try_strptime(sent_at, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f %z')::TIMESTAMP)), TIMESTAMP '2016-01-01') AS start_date
    FROM staging.stg_qualtrics__distribution_contact
    WHERE try_strptime(sent_at, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f %z')::TIMESTAMP IS NOT NULL
),
date_spine AS (
    SELECT unnest(generate_series(start_date, date_trunc('day', current_timestamp) + INTERVAL 7 DAY, INTERVAL 1 DAY))::TIMESTAMP AS date_day
    FROM spine_bounds
)
SELECT
    date_spine.date_day,
    coalesce(contact_events.count_contacts_created, 0)::BIGINT AS count_contacts_created,
    coalesce(unsubscribe_directory_daily.count_contacts_unsubscribed_from_directory, 0)::BIGINT AS count_contacts_unsubscribed_from_directory,
    coalesce(unsubscribe_mailing_list_daily.count_contacts_unsubscribed_from_mailing_list, 0)::BIGINT AS count_contacts_unsubscribed_from_mailing_list,

    coalesce(response_daily.count_social_media_completed_survey_responses, 0)::BIGINT AS count_social_media_completed_survey_responses,
    coalesce(response_daily.count_personal_link_survey_responses, 0)::BIGINT AS count_personal_link_survey_responses,
    coalesce(response_daily.count_personal_link_completed_survey_responses, 0)::BIGINT AS count_personal_link_completed_survey_responses,
    coalesce(response_daily.count_qr_code_survey_responses, 0)::BIGINT AS count_qr_code_survey_responses,
    coalesce(response_daily.count_qr_code_completed_survey_responses, 0)::BIGINT AS count_qr_code_completed_survey_responses,
    coalesce(response_daily.count_email_survey_responses, 0)::BIGINT AS count_email_survey_responses,
    coalesce(response_daily.count_email_completed_survey_responses, 0)::BIGINT AS count_email_completed_survey_responses,
    coalesce(response_daily.count_sms_survey_responses, 0)::BIGINT AS count_sms_survey_responses,
    coalesce(response_daily.count_sms_completed_survey_responses, 0)::BIGINT AS count_sms_completed_survey_responses,

        count(DISTINCT contact_id) FILTER (WHERE is_unsubscribed_from_directory IS TRUE)::BIGINT AS total_count_unsubscribed_contacts,
        count(DISTINCT contact_id) FILTER (WHERE created_at >= current_timestamp - INTERVAL 30 DAY AND created_at <= current_timestamp)::BIGINT AS count_contacts_created_30d,
        count(DISTINCT contact_id) FILTER (WHERE is_unsubscribed_from_directory IS TRUE AND unsubscribed_from_directory_at >= current_timestamp - INTERVAL 30 DAY AND unsubscribed_from_directory_at <= current_timestamp)::BIGINT AS count_contacts_unsubscribed_30d
    FROM staging.stg_qualtrics__directory_contact
    GROUP BY directory_id
),
mailing_list_aggregates AS (
    SELECT directory_id, count(DISTINCT mailing_list_id)::BIGINT AS count_mailing_lists
    FROM staging.stg_qualtrics__directory_mailing_list
    GROUP BY directory_id
),
distribution_events AS (
    SELECT
        directory_contact.directory_id,
        distribution_contact.contact_id,
        distribution.survey_id,
        try_strptime(distribution_contact.sent_at, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f %z')::TIMESTAMP AS sent_at,
        try_strptime(distribution_contact.opened_at, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f %z')::TIMESTAMP AS opened_at,
        try_strptime(distribution_contact.response_started_at, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f %z')::TIMESTAMP AS response_started_at,
        try_strptime(distribution_contact.response_completed_at, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f %z')::TIMESTAMP AS response_completed_at
    FROM staging.stg_qualtrics__distribution_contact AS distribution_contact
    INNER JOIN staging.stg_qualtrics__directory_contact AS directory_contact
        ON distribution_contact.contact_id = directory_contact.contact_id
    LEFT JOIN staging.stg_qualtrics__distribution AS distribution
        ON distribution_contact.distribution_id = distribution.distribution_id
),
distribution_aggregates AS (
    SELECT
        directory_id,
        count(DISTINCT contact_id) FILTER (WHERE sent_at IS NOT NULL)::BIGINT AS count_contacts_sent_survey_30d,

      grain: One row per survey_id with total_responses > 0
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_qualtrics__survey_performance
      - intermediate.int_qualtrics__response_quality

WITH eligible_responses AS (
    SELECT
        coalesce(recipient_email, 'anonymous_' || response_id) AS user_identifier,
        response_id,
        is_finished,
        try_strptime(recorded_date, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f %z')::TIMESTAMP AS recorded_at
    FROM staging.stg_qualtrics__survey_response
    WHERE recorded_date IS NOT NULL
),
user_metrics AS (
    SELECT
        user_identifier,
        date_trunc('month', min(recorded_at))::DATE AS cohort_month,
        count(DISTINCT response_id)::BIGINT AS total_responses,
        count(DISTINCT response_id) FILTER (WHERE is_finished IS TRUE)::BIGINT AS completed_responses
    FROM eligible_responses
    WHERE recorded_at IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY user_identifier
),
user_tiers AS (
    SELECT
        *,
        completed_responses::DOUBLE / nullif(total_responses, 0) * 100 AS completion_rate,
        CASE
            WHEN total_responses >= 20 THEN 'Power User'
            WHEN total_responses >= 10 THEN 'High Value'
            WHEN total_responses >= 5 THEN 'Medium Value'
            WHEN total_responses >= 2 THEN 'Low Value'
            ELSE 'One-time User'
        END AS user_value_tier
    FROM user_metrics
),
cohort_metrics AS (
    SELECT
        cohort_month,
        count(DISTINCT user_identifier)::BIGINT AS cohort_size,
        avg(total_responses)::DOUBLE AS avg_responses_per_user,
        avg(completion_rate)::DOUBLE AS avg_completion_rate,
        count(*) FILTER (WHERE user_value_tier = 'Power User')::BIGINT AS power_users,
        count(*) FILTER (WHERE user_value_tier = 'High Value')::BIGINT AS high_value_users,
        count(*) FILTER (WHERE user_value_tier = 'Medium Value')::BIGINT AS medium_value_users,
        count(*) FILTER (WHERE user_value_tier = 'Low Value')::BIGINT AS low_value_users,
        count(*) FILTER (WHERE user_value_tier = 'One-time User')::BIGINT AS one_time_users
    FROM user_tiers
    GROUP BY cohort_month
)
SELECT
    cohort_month,
    cohort_size,
    avg_responses_per_user,
    avg_completion_rate,
    power_users,
    high_value_users,
    medium_value_users,
    low_value_users,
    one_time_users,
    0.6 * avg_completion_rate + 40.0 * (power_users + high_value_users)::DOUBLE / cohort_size AS cohort_health_score
FROM cohort_metrics
WHERE cohort_size > 0
ORDER BY cohort_month DESC

cte_definitions.name: user_metrics
cte_definitions.sql: SELECT user_identifier, CAST(DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', MIN(recorded_at)) AS DATE) AS cohort_month, CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT response_id) AS BIGINT) AS total_responses, CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT response_id) FILTER(WHERE is_finished IS TRUE) AS BIGINT) AS completed_responses FROM eligible_responses WHERE NOT recorded_at IS NULL GROUP BY user_identifier

cte_definitions.name: user_tiers
cte_definitions.sql: SELECT *, CAST(completed_responses AS DOUBLE) / NULLIF(total_responses, 0) * 100 AS completion_rate, CASE WHEN total_responses >= 20 THEN 'Power User' WHEN total_responses >= 10 THEN 'High Value' WHEN total_responses >= 5 THEN 'Medium Value' WHEN total_responses >= 2 THEN 'Low Value' ELSE 'One-time User' END AS user_value_tier FROM user_metrics

cte_definitions.name: cohort_metrics
cte_definitions.sql: SELECT cohort_month, CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT user_identifier) AS BIGINT) AS cohort_size, CAST(AVG(total_responses) AS DOUBLE) AS avg_responses_per_user, CAST(AVG(completion_rate) AS DOUBLE) AS avg_completion_rate, CAST(COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE user_value_tier = 'Power User') AS BIGINT) AS power_users, CAST(COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE user_value_tier = 'High Value') AS BIGINT) AS high_value_users, CAST(COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE user_value_tier = 'Medium Value') AS BIGINT) AS medium_value_users, CAST(COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE user_value_tier = 'Low Value') AS BIGINT) AS low_value_users, CAST(COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE user_value_tier = 'One-time User') AS BIGINT) AS one_time_users FROM user_tiers GROUP BY cohort_month

blocks.original_text:
- name: qualtrics__user_cohort_analysis
      description: 'Monthly user cohort metrics from Qualtrics responses: cohort size, per-user averages, value-tier counts, and a 0–100 health score'
      grain: One row per cohort_month
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_qualtrics__survey_response
      business_logic: 'Build cohorts from staging.stg_qualtrics__survey_response: - Keep only records with recorded_date present. - Define user_identifier: use recipient_email when available; otherwise use the literal prefix "anonymous_" followed by response_id. - Per user_identifier: - first_response_date: the earliest timestamp parsed from recorded_date. - cohort_month: the first calendar day of the month of first_response_date. - total_responses: count of distinct response_id. - completed_responses: count of distinct response_id where is_finished is true (null/false excluded). - completion_rate (percent): if total_responses > 0, completed_responses / total_responses × 100; otherwise 0. Use decimal division. - user_value_tier by total_responses: ≥20 Power User; ≥10 High Value; ≥5 Medium Value; ≥2 Low Value; else One-time User. Aggregate by cohort_month: - cohort_size: distinct users in the cohort. - avg_responses_per_user: average of per-user total_responses. - avg_completion_rate: average of per-user completion_rate (percent). - power_users/high_value_users/medium_value_users/low_value_users/one_time_users: counts of users in each tier. - cohort_health_score: 0.6 × avg_completion_rate + 40 × (count of Power or High Value users ÷ cohort_size). Expected range 0–100. Finalize: - Exclude cohorts where cohort_size = 0. - Return one row per cohort_month; sorted descending by cohort_month (sorting does not affect values).'
      columns:
      - name: cohort_month
        data_type: DATE
        description: First day of the month of each user's first response; cohort grouping key.
      - name: cohort_size
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of distinct users in the cohort_month.
      - name: avg_responses_per_user
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Mean per-user count of distinct responses within the cohort.
      - name: avg_completion_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Mean per-user completion rate in percent, where per-user rate is completed distinct responses divided by total distinct responses times 100.
      - name: power_users
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Count of users with total_responses ≥ 20 in the cohort.
      - name: high_value_users
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Count of users with total_responses ≥ 10 and < 20 in the cohort.
      - name: medium_value_users
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Count of users with total_responses ≥ 5 and < 10 in the cohort.
      - name: low_value_users
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Count of users with total_responses ≥ 2 and < 5 in the cohort.
      - name: one_time_users
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Count of users with total_responses = 1 in the cohort.
      - name: cohort_health_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: '0–100 score: 0.6×avg_completion_rate + 40×(share of Power or High Value users in the cohort).'
